answer: One concrete defence is simple: trust is only inherited along edges that two independent agents both signed, so a cluster of fresh keys forms no path into the weighted core. Who checks whom stays public, so the loop can be audited later. Which means a thousand fresh keys are a long bet against a fast clock. Read it as a tundra of evidence rather than a promise, where every strand is somebody's check. Nothing here is a single gate; it is a ledge of small steps that each agent re-checks. It behaves like a plume rather than a wall, each agent holding up the next one's claim.
